extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark that covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It introduces a novel static-to-dynamic method to define temporal-related tasks, and automatically converts public video annotations into multiple-choice QA to evaluate each task. The benchmark covers a wide range of temporal understanding skills from perception to cognition, using videos from 11 public datasets.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.publisher: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology (Chinese Academy of Sciences), University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Nanjing University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos are collected from 11 existing public video benchmarks covering various complex domains and diverse scenes, ranging from first-person to third-person perspectives, and from indoor to outdoor environments. The benchmark uses a static-to-dynamic method to define temporal tasks, and an automatic QA generation paradigm to convert public video annotations into multiple-choice QAs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1 (MiT V1), FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR, the challenge is enhanced by randomly shifting the start or end points of video clips to increase the complexity of localizing specific events. For CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions for describing specific events are excluded to decrease QA difficulty. Videos with intermediate duration (primarily 5s to 35s) are selected to ensure temporal sensitivity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration involves three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: selecting from 11 video datasets covering broad domains and scenes; (2) Temporal Sensitivity: eliminating short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos, selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s; (3) Question Difficulty: designing selection criteria for STAR and CLEVRER to balance question difficulty. Answer options are randomly sampled (3 to 5 options) and shuffled. LLM is used to ensure all answer options of a question are of similar and reasonable lengths.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An automatic QA generation paradigm is used to convert open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QAs. Two approaches are used: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates are constructed directly from ground truth annotations; (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT is used to generate questions based on task definitions and to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice QA with answer options. 200 multiple-choice QA pairs are produced for each temporal understanding task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The multiple-choice format is used instead of open-ended format to ensure evaluation correctness and fairness, avoiding biased scoring by LLMs or manual intervention. Ground-truth video annotations from public benchmarks are used to guarantee evaluation fairness and accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 multiple-choice QA pair per video (200 QA pairs per task, 20 tasks total = 4000 QA pairs)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT (used for question generation, option generation, and converting open-ended QAs to multiple-choice format); UMT-L/16 (used for generating top-6 action predictions as answer candidates for Fine-grained Action task)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A leaderboard is maintained at https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenGVLab/MVBench_Leaderboard. All models and data are publicly available at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MVBench aims to comprehensively evaluate the temporal perception capabilities of MLLMs in the open world, helping to identify gaps in current models' temporal understanding and directing future improvements in video MLLM design.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There is a minimal source gap between the instruction tuning data and MVBench. Specifically, CLEVRER in the instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference tasks in MVBench, and videos of Action Antonym are from SthSthV2 while the antonym is from PAXION, meaning evaluation is not strictly out-of-domain for these tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs have difficulty generalizing to localization and counting tasks in the absence of related tuning data. The benchmark reveals that existing MLLMs are far from satisfactory in temporal understanding. Visual information alone may not be sufficient for complex cognition tasks such as egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning, suggesting that other modalities (depth, audio) could be beneficial.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on temporal understanding capabilities in video. The benchmark is designed to evaluate 20 challenging video tasks covering perception to cognition, including action, object, position, scene, count, attribute, pose, character, and cognition tasks.
